novel_features.name: Stale quotes
novel_features.description: List Open estimates older than N days, ranked by age × total $ so the biggest-dollar stuck quotes surface first.
novel_features.rationale: No ST API call sorts Open estimates by computed (now − createdOn) × total. Requires the local SQLite mirror.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to find quotes the sales team has let go cold. Cheaper than walking the ST web UI page-by-page.

novel_features.name: Rep leaderboard
novel_features.description: Per-employee close rate, average days-to-sell, and total sold $ for the chosen window.
novel_features.rationale: Joins estimates × status_changes and aggregates by soldById; not a single API call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when an agent or owner needs to compare sales reps on close performance without pivoting in Excel.

novel_features.name: Close rate
novel_features.description: sold/(sold+dismissed) pivoted on businessUnit, rep, or month with a configurable date window.
novel_features.rationale: Requires SQLite GROUP BY across estimates and status_changes; the API has no equivalent.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to answer 'what's our close rate by business unit this quarter?' in one MCP turn instead of a 400-tool ST MCP query.

novel_features.name: Days to sell
novel_features.description: p50/p90 percentiles of (Sold timestamp − createdOn) per rep or business unit.
novel_features.rationale: Needs min(status_changes.changedAtUTC WHERE toStatus='Sold') joined to estimates.createdOn, then percentile math.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to spot reps whose long-tail close time is dragging pipeline velocity.

novel_features.name: Dismissed reasons
novel_features.description: Top-N exact-match group-by on dismissal reason strings from the status-change feed.
novel_features.rationale: Mechanical count over status_changes; no NLP; the API has no grouped-by-reason endpoint.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to see what's killing deals (price, timing, scope) so the next sales script iteration addresses it.

novel_features.name: Estimate audit
novel_features.description: Single estimate forensic view — header + every line item + full status timeline in one shaped output.
novel_features.rationale: Three local SELECTs joined into one struct (estimate × items × status_changes); the API returns each separately.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when a CSR needs to explain to a customer 'what happened with quote 78421' without four ST web tabs.

novel_features.name: Recent changes
novel_features.description: Every estimate whose status changed in a time window with from→to + actor + UTC timestamp.
novel_features.rationale: SQLite JOIN status_changes (where changedAtUTC > now-window) with estimates header; no equivalent in any single API call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use first thing in the morning to triage overnight sold/dismissed/unsold activity.

novel_features.name: Find
novel_features.description: Ranked full-text search across estimate name, summary, jobNumber, and nested SKU fields with structured filters.
novel_features.rationale: Scored ranking over multi-table SQLite fields; the ST list endpoint does not full-text across nested line items.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when the customer's phrase is the only handle you have on a quote.

novel_features.name: Pipeline snapshot
novel_features.description: Total $ Open / Sold / Dismissed reconstructed for an arbitrary past date by replaying status_changes.
novel_features.rationale: Temporal reconstruction from the status-change event log; the API only returns current state.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to answer 'where was pipeline last Monday?' without a manual snapshot job.

novel_features.name: Health
novel_features.description: Cross-source reconciliation — API counts vs local SQLite counts vs last sync cursor age per table.
novel_features.rationale: Calls list endpoints with limit=1 to fetch totalCount; diffs against SQLite COUNT(*); reports cursor age.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use as a pre-flight check before any audit so you know whether the local mirror is fresh enough to trust.

novel_features.name: SKU frequency
novel_features.description: Top SKUs by appearance on sold (or dismissed) estimates in a time window.
novel_features.rationale: Joins estimate_items × estimates filtered by status; the API only returns items per single estimate.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to inform pricebook decisions — which SKUs are actually carrying sold dollars.

novel_features.name: Rep follow-ups
novel_features.description: Per-rep open estimates from the last N hours with customerId, jobId/jobNumber, and ST web deeplinks — the daily call list for follow-up outreach.
novel_features.rationale: Joins estimates × status_changes filtered to Open + created in window, grouped by soldById; no single API call returns this rep-grouped follow-up view.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to generate today's call list per rep. Pipe customerId into `servicetitan-crm-pp-cli customers get <id>` to enrich with phone numbers.

novel_features.name: Record follow-up
novel_features.description: Log a follow-up note + optional reminder date against an estimate into the local SQLite store, then list follow-ups due by date.
novel_features.rationale: The ST API has no estimate-notes endpoint — this is a pure local-write feature filling the gap so follow-up state survives across calls.
novel_features.example: servicetitan-salestech-pp-cli audit follow-up add 78421 --note "customer wants to talk Monday" --remind 2026-05-20
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to keep follow-up state next to the estimate it belongs to, so 'who needs a callback this week' is one local SQL query away.

novel_features.name: CSV → estimate import
novel_features.description: Read a defined CSV schema and create estimates with line items in ServiceTitan, with --dry-run preview and --batch-size flow control.
novel_features.rationale: Combines Estimates_Create + Estimates_PutItem calls per CSV row with row-level error reporting; no single API call accepts a sheet.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to convert an Excel/Google Sheets quote into a real ServiceTitan estimate without copy-pasting field by field. Export the sheet to CSV first; XLSX and Google Sheets are documented v2 paths.

narrative.headline: Every ServiceTitan Sales/Estimates feature, plus a local mirror that answers the cross-cutting questions the ST web UI never could.
narrative.value_prop: Wraps all 13 Sales/Estimates endpoints (plus a convenience `estimates reopen`) with agent-native JSON, --select dotted paths, --csv, and typed exit codes. Then adds 14 hand-built audits and workflow commands (stale, leaderboard, close-rate, days-to-sell, dismissed-reasons, pipeline-snapshot, recent-changes, audit, find, health, sku-frequency, rep follow-ups, local follow-up logging, CSV→estimate import) that compose locally over a SQLite mirror — every question a pipeline review meeting asks, plus the daily follow-up call list and a way to ingest sheet-based quotes, in one command. The matching MCP collapses 14 endpoint tools to 2 intent tools so agents pay near-zero per-turn context tax.
narrative.auth_narrative: Composed auth — both ST_APP_KEY (apiKey header) and an OAuth2 client_credentials bearer are required on every call. Set ST_APP_KEY, ST_CLIENT_ID, ST_CLIENT_SECRET, and ST_TENANT_ID, then run `auth login` to mint the bearer. `doctor` verifies all four are present and reachable. Whitespace is stripped defensively from every env var (a known JKA gotcha that produced opaque invalid_client 400s).

quickstart.comment: Verify all four ST_* env vars are set and the OAuth handshake works
Exchange ST_CLIENT_ID/SECRET for an OAuth2 bearer token cached locally
Pull estimates, line items, and status changes into the local SQLite mirror
Surface Open estimates that have aged past 3 days, sorted by age × total $
Per-rep close rate + avg days-to-sell + sold $
Single-estimate forensic: header + items + full status timeline
Today's call list per rep — open estimates from the last 48h with customerId + jobNumber + deeplinks

troubleshoots.fix: Run `doctor` — most often ST_APP_KEY is missing from this shell. Composed auth needs BOTH ST_APP_KEY and the OAuth bearer; the bearer alone is not enough.

One of ST_CLIENT_ID / ST_CLIENT_SECRET has stray whitespace. The CLI strips it defensively, but confirm both shells (PowerShell vs git-bash) see the same value by comparing **lengths** only — `python -c "import os;print('id',len(os.environ['ST_CLIENT_ID']),'sec',len(os.environ['ST_CLIENT_SECRET']))"` — and refresh the stale shell.
Verify ST_TENANT_ID is set — without it the {tenant} path template stays unfilled and every list call 404s.

troubleshoots.symptom: `reports pipeline --as-of <old-date>` returns a warning about retention
troubleshoots.fix: Status-change retention on the ST tenant is shorter than the requested as-of date; the snapshot uses the oldest available baseline and notes the gap. Pull more recent dates for accurate point-in-time totals.
Check that the launching process exports all four ST_* env vars; the MCP inherits its env from the parent (Claude Desktop reads `claude_desktop_config.json`'s `env` block, NOT live OS env).

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for this CLI when an agent or user needs to answer a cross-cutting estimates question that the ST web UI buries — close rates, stale quotes, days-to-sell distributions, dismissed-reason patterns, point-in-time pipeline state, or any forensic lookup of a single estimate's full history. The 13 endpoint mirrors cover write-side work too, but the headline value is the 14 local-mirror audits. If you only need to read or update one specific estimate by id, the absorbed `estimates get/update/sell/unsell/dismiss/reopen` commands are the right reach; if you need to know something about the whole pipeline, the `reports` and `audit` families are.

recipes.title: Monday pipeline review
recipes.explanation: Per-rep close rate + avg days-to-sell + sold $ for the year. Pipe to jq to filter the result, e.g. `... | jq '.[] | select(.close_rate < 0.4)'` flags reps below a 40% close rate for coaching.

recipes.title: Triage overnight activity
recipes.explanation: See every estimate whose status moved in the last 24h with only the fields the dispatcher cares about; --select keeps the response under a few KB even when 200+ estimates moved.

recipes.title: Find a quote by customer phrase
recipes.explanation: FTS5 across name, summary, jobNumber, and SKU fields filtered to Open quotes over $5k.

recipes.title: Forensic on one estimate
recipes.explanation: Header + every line item + full status timeline in one shaped JSON object — perfect for an agent to explain 'what happened' to a customer.

recipes.title: Historical pipeline check
recipes.explanation: Reconstruct end-of-month pipeline totals by replaying status_changes; impossible via any single ST API call.

recipes.title: Build today's rep call list (with phone enrichment)
recipes.explanation: Today's call list per rep with customerId + jobNumber + ST deeplinks. The Sales/Estimates spec deliberately omits customer contact data — enrich by piping each row's customer_id into `servicetitan-crm-pp-cli customers get <id> --json | jq -r .phoneSettings.phoneNumber`.

recipes.title: Reopen a dismissed estimate
recipes.explanation: Wraps Estimates_Update with status=Open to reverse a dismiss. Drop --dry-run when you're ready to commit.

recipes.title: Log a follow-up reminder
recipes.command: servicetitan-salestech-pp-cli audit follow-up add 78421 --note "customer asked us to follow up Monday" --remind 2026-05-20
recipes.explanation: Writes to the local SQLite store only; later `audit follow-ups --due-by 2026-05-21` surfaces it.

recipes.title: Import an Excel quote (via CSV export)
recipes.explanation: Export your Excel/Sheets quote to CSV first, then dry-run to preview the Estimates_Create + line-item calls. Drop --dry-run to commit.
